context_requirements: Expression of serotonin receptors (HTR2A/HTR2B/HTR2C/HTR1A/HTR1B/HTR1D/HTR3A/HTR3B/HTR4/HTR6/HTR7) or ADRA1A on the cell line
Active serotonin/5-HT autocrine or paracrine signaling driving proliferation
Intact Gq/PLC-Ca2+ and MAPK signaling downstream of HTR2/HTR1 receptors
Proliferative drive dependent on cyclin D / MYC for antagonists to show anti-proliferative effects
falsifiers: No change in cyclin D1/D3, MYC, or proliferation gene expression at 24 h in any line
No G1 arrest or apoptosis signature at 24 h
Strong and reproducible transcriptional response in HA1E (a non-tumor line) comparable to cancer lines
Upregulation of proliferation genes rather than downregulation
No difference between 6 h and 24 h responses (would contradict slow kinetics)

evidence.supports: Methiothepin, a serotonin receptor antagonist, suppresses ovarian cancer cell viability, induces apoptosis and mitochondrial/metabolic dysfunction
Cyproheptadine decreases cyclin D1/D2/D3, causes G0/G1 arrest and apoptosis in myeloma and leukemia cells, though this effect was reported independent of serotonin receptor antagonism
Sarpogrelate, a specific serotonin receptor antagonist, inhibits serotonin-induced proliferation of vascular smooth muscle cells
